Port3 Network's BNB Chain token suffered a bridge contract exploit on November 23, 2025. An attacker minted 1 billion unauthorized PORT3 tokens due to a logic error triggered by a flawed ownership check after contract ownership was renounced. About 162.75 million PORT3 tokens were sold for ~$166,000, crashing the token price. The remainder were burned. Exchange listings paused and a new token contract was announced. A logic flaw in the adopted CATERC20 cross-chain contract allowed the owner check to pass when ownership was renounced (set to zero address), letting the attacker register a fake chain and invoke an unrestricted mint via BridgeIn.
